questions.question: Why can the diagrams of cells in textbooks sometimes be misleading about their actual shape?
options: They show cells as flat 2D shapes, but real cells have a 3D shape.
They show cells with cell walls, but real cells never have walls.
They suggest cells are much larger than they really are.
They only show cells in black and white.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is found in typical animal cells?
options: Chloroplast
Cell wall
Mitochondria
Large permanent vacuole

questions.question: What is the primary function of the cell membrane in an animal cell?
options: To release energy through aerobic respiration
To control the movement of substances in and out of the cell
To store genetic information and control cell activities
To provide a rigid outer support structure

questions.question: Which statement best describes a unicellular organism?
options: An organism that does not have any cells.
An organism made up of a single living cell.
An organism that has tissues but no organs.
An organism made of millions of different cells.

questions.question: How do multicellular organisms differ from unicellular organisms?
options: They are made of more than one cell, with different cells taking on different jobs.
They contain only one large cell that performs all life processes.
They do not require nutrition or respiration to survive.
They are made of cells that are all completely identical in function.

questions.question: In multicellular organisms, what is formed when a group of similar cells join together to perform a specific job?
options: An organ system
A tissue
An organism
A chloroplast

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes how organs and organ systems are organized?
options: An organ is a single cell that works completely on its own.
An organ is made of different organ systems working together.
An organ is a group of tissues working together, and organs work together in an organ system.
Tissues work together to form cells, which then form an organ.

questions.question: What are the fundamental living building blocks that make up all organisms?
options: Atoms
Tissues
Cells
Organs

questions.question: Why do we typically need a microscope to study individual cells?
options: Cells are usually too small to see with the unaided eye.
Cells only exist when light shines on them.
Cells are completely transparent and cannot reflect light.
Cells move too fast to be seen by human eyes.

questions.question: Which scientific instrument is commonly used in a school laboratory to observe the cells that make up a tissue slide?
options: A hand lens
A telescope
A light microscope
A magnifying glass

questions.question: Which of these structures would you expect to find in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
options: Cell wall and vacuole
Cytoplasm and nucleus
Cell membrane and mitochondria
Nucleus and cytoplasm

questions.question: When preparing a slide of plant or animal cells, why might a scientist add a stain?
options: To kill any harmful bacteria on the slide
To glue the coverslip permanently to the slide
To make it easier to see some parts of the cells
To make the cells grow larger under the lens

questions.question: What is a key feature of specialised cells in animals and plants?
options: They all have the exact same shape and size.
They are only found in unicellular organisms.
They have shapes, sizes, and structures adapted for the specific jobs they do.
They lose their cell membranes as they mature.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a specialised plant cell?
options: Red blood cell
Root hair cell
Muscle cell
Nerve cell

questions.question: Which of the following lists represents actual life processes that happen in all living organisms?
options: Movement, reproduction, sensitivity, growth, respiration, excretion and nutrition
Thinking, sleeping, talking, walking, breathing and hearing
Photosynthesis, circulation, digestion, running and crying
Melting, freezing, evaporating, condensing and dissolving

questions.question: In the context of life processes, when is movement considered a true sign of life?
options: When the organism is blown by the wind
When the organism is carried by water currents
When the organism moves itself to achieve something
When the organism is pushed by an external force

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the common structures of plant cells?
options: Plant cells share no common structures with animal cells.
Plant cells have some common structures, such as a nucleus and cell membrane.
Plant cells lack a cytoplasm completely.
Plant cells only contain chloroplasts and have no other structures.

questions.question: How should observations of cells from a light microscope be recorded in a scientific report?
options: By drawing a colorful, abstract painting
By writing a detailed fictional story
In a clear, scientific line drawing
By memory without looking at the slide
